title: Cap. VI Arg. 12: first — Quisquis decree stands even if none or all believe; Peter = Judas
pass_a_gloss: First, because this decree would stand firm and immovable, even if no one believed, even if all perished; and on the contrary, even if all believed, and all were saved. By such a decree therefore, after the manner of a law or Edict, it is declared by what duties performed it is lawful for anyone to approach eternal life, by which neglected it is not lawful: but meantime, after the manner of a practical and segregative decree, no one is segregated or elected before others, no one is passed by or left. For if Judas shall have believed and persevered, by virtue of this decree he will be saved: If Peter shall not have believed and persevered, by virtue of the same he will be damned. Nothing is here decreed for Peter that is not under the same condition decreed for Judas; nothing is denied Judas that is not under the same condition denied Peter. By equal law and condition, if we cling to this decree, all are destined to salvation, all are excluded from salvation. There is therefore in this decree no segregation of singular persons, or election with others passed by.
pass_b_english: First: that decree would stand firm even if no one believed and all perished — or if all believed and all were saved. As law or edict it declares by what duties done anyone may come to eternal life, and by what neglected may not. But as a practical segregating decree, no one is set apart or chosen before others, no one passed by. If Judas believes and perseveres, by it he is saved; if Peter does not, by the same he is damned. Nothing is decreed for Peter not under the same condition for Judas; nothing denied Judas not under the same for Peter. Cling to that decree on equal law, and all are destined to salvation and all excluded from it. So there is no segregation of singulars, no election with others passed by.
source_text: Primo, quia staret hoc decretum firmum et immobile, etiamsi nemo crederet, etiamsi omnes perirent; et e contra, etiamsi omnes crederent, et omnes servarentur. Tali ergo decreto, per modum legis aut Edicti, declaratur quibus officiis praestitis liceat cuilibet vitam aeternam adire, quibus neglectis non liceat: at interim, per modum decreti practici et segregativi, nemo segregatur aut prae aliis eligitur, nemo praeteritur aut relinquitur. Si enim Judas crediderit et perseveraverit, virtute hujus decreti servabitur: Si Petrus non crediderit et perseveraverit, virtute ejusdem damnabitur. Nihil hic decernitur Petro, quod non sub eadem conditione decernitur Judae; nihil negatur Judae, quod non sub eadem conditione negatur Petro. Pari lege et conditione, huic decreto inhaereamus, omnes destinantur ad salutem, omnes excluduntur a salute. Nulla igitur in hoc decreto singularium personarum segregatio, aut aliis praeteritis electio.
